note: Quotes from works in the public domain. Length groups are derived from character count at runtime.

quotes.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.text: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago, never mind how long precisely, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world.
quotes.author: Herman Melville

quotes.text: Why, sometimes I have believed as many as six impossible things before breakfast.
quotes.author: Lewis Carroll

quotes.text: If you do not know where you are going, any road will take you there.
quotes.author: Lewis Carroll

quotes.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau

quotes.text: You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts, so guard accordingly, and take care that you entertain no notions unsuitable to virtue.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: This above all: to thine own self be true, and it must follow, as the night the day, thou canst not then be false to any man.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: It is a capital mistake to theorize before you have all the evidence. It biases the judgment.
quotes.author: Arthur Conan Doyle

quotes.text: When you have eliminated all which is impossible, then whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.
quotes.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
quotes.source: The Case Book of Sherlock Holmes

quotes.text: Nothing is so painful to the human mind as a great and sudden change.
quotes.author: Mary Shelley

quotes.text: The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it. Resist it, and your soul grows sick with longing for the things it has forbidden to itself.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.text: Experience is merely the name men gave to their mistakes.
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.text: It was kind of solemn, drifting down the big still river, laying on our backs looking up at the stars, and we did not ever feel like talking loud.
quotes.author: Mark Twain

quotes.text: The secret of getting ahead is getting started.
quotes.author: Mark Twain

quotes.text: It is not the strongest of the species that survives, nor the most intelligent, but the one most responsive to change.
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.text: In the midst of chaos, there is also opportunity. He who knows when he can fight and when he cannot will be victorious.
quotes.author: Sun Tzu

quotes.text: To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

quotes.text: It is not down on any map; true places never are.
quotes.author: Herman Melville

quotes.text: Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same, and the other is as different as a moonbeam from lightning, or frost from fire.
quotes.author: Emily Bronte

quotes.text: I am no bird; and no net ensnares me: I am a free human being with an independent will.
quotes.author: Charlotte Bronte

quotes.text: We can know only that we know nothing. And that is the highest degree of human wisdom.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.text: Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.text: Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart. The really great men must, I think, have great sadness on earth.
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.text: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
quotes.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

quotes.text: I cannot make you understand. I cannot make anyone understand what is happening inside me. I cannot even explain it to myself.
quotes.author: Franz Kafka

quotes.text: Keep your face always toward the sunshine, and shadows will fall behind you.
quotes.author: Walt Whitman

quotes.text: A man of genius makes no mistakes. His errors are the portals of discovery.
quotes.author: James Joyce

quotes.text: The moment you doubt whether you can fly, you cease forever to be able to do it.
quotes.author: J. M. Barrie

quotes.text: There is no difference between time and any of the three dimensions of space except that our consciousness moves along it.
quotes.author: H. G. Wells

quotes.text: I am not afraid of storms, for I am learning how to sail my ship.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott

quotes.text: It is a narrow mind which cannot look at a subject from various points of view.
quotes.author: George Eliot
